class.name: SnowFall3D
class.brief_description: Falling and blowing snow around the camera, from the weather and the snowpack.
class.description: GPU particles in a box around the camera, drawn in raster and traced under path tracing. The snowfall comes from the [SnowCover3D] (the weather's precipitation, as snow where it is cold enough at that height). Flakes follow the measured size distribution of snowfall (Gunn and Marshall 1958) and fall at the measured speed of snowflake aggregates (Locatelli and Hobbs 1974), carried by the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] wind at their height, with its gusts and shelter, and flutter on small zigzag and spiral paths. A heightfield collider keeps them off the ground under roofs and trees. Each flake is drawn as a quad stretched along its motion during [member streak_time], keeping its light when it is smaller than a pixel. Above the threshold wind of dry snow (Li and Pomeroy 1997), snow blows off the pack: grains hop in a shallow saltation layer and finer snow drifts higher, moving with the wind profile, in an amount that follows the saltation flux (Pomeroy 1989), only over loose dry snow. The snowfall beyond the box is left to fog: [method get_extinction] gives the extinction of the current snowfall.

method.name: blowing_concentration
method.description: Mass concentration of suspended blowing snow (kg/m³) at [param height] metres over the snow in a [param wind10] m/s wind at 10 m (Pomeroy and Male 1992).

method.name: blowing_extinction
method.description: Extinction per metre of blowing snow of [param concentration] kg/m³ (geometric optics, 40 µm grains).

method.name: get_blowing_extinction
method.description: The blowing snow's extinction at 1 m over the snow under the camera, per metre (0 when none blows).

method.name: get_blowing_height_scale
method.description: The e-folding height of the blowing-snow haze, in metres.

method.name: blowing_threshold
method.description: Returns the 10 m wind speed in m/s above which dry snow starts to blow, [code]9.43 + 0.18 T + 0.0033 T^2[/code] (Li and Pomeroy 1997).

method.name: fall_speed
method.description: Returns the fall speed in m/s of a snowflake [param size] millimetres across, [code]0.8 D^0.16[/code] (Locatelli and Hobbs 1974, aggregates of dendrites).

method.name: flake_number_density
method.description: Returns the number of flakes per cubic metre larger than [param min_size] millimetres in snowfall of [param rate] millimetres of water an hour (Gunn and Marshall 1958, flake size from melted size by Magono and Nakamura 1965).

method.name: flake_size_slope
method.description: Returns the slope of the Gunn and Marshall size distribution, [code]2.55 R^-0.48[/code] per millimetre of melted diameter.

method.name: get_blowing_amount
method.description: Returns the share of [member max_blowing] shown, from the saltation flux.

method.name: get_extinction
method.description: Returns the extinction of light by the current snowfall, per metre. Feed it to the fog density so the snowfall beyond the particle box reads as haze.

method.name: get_snowfall_rate
method.description: Returns the snowfall at the box centre, in millimetres of water an hour.

method.name: get_threshold_wind
method.description: Returns the threshold wind for blowing snow in use, in m/s at 10 m.

method.name: get_visibility
method.description: Returns the visibility through the current snowfall in metres, [code]3.912 / extinction[/code] (Koschmieder).

method.name: get_visible_flakes
method.description: Returns the number of flakes shown.

method.name: get_wind_speed_10m
method.description: Returns the wind speed at 10 m over the ground under the box, in m/s.

method.name: saltation_flux_ratio
method.description: Returns the saltation flux at [param wind10] relative to the flux at 1.5 times [param threshold]: [code]u^3 (1 - ut^2 / u^2)[/code] (Pomeroy 1989), 0 below the threshold.

method.name: snowfall_extinction
method.description: Returns the extinction per metre of snowfall at [param rate] millimetres of water an hour, from the flake size distribution with an extinction efficiency of 2: about 2 km of visibility at 1 mm/h and 200 m at 3 mm/h.

members.member: The width of the blowing snow area around the box centre, in metres.
If [code]true[/code], snow blows off loose dry snow when the wind is above [method get_threshold_wind].
Scales the amount of blowing snow.
Scales the number of flakes from the measured number density.
The box of falling flakes around the camera (or [member follow_target]), in metres. Beyond it, use [method get_extinction] for fog.
If [code]true[/code], flakes fall from the snowfall at the camera.
Scales the drawn size of the flakes.
The node the boxes follow. Empty: the current camera.
The number of blowing snow particles at full strength.
The number of flake particles; heavy snowfall is capped at it.
The smallest flake drawn, in millimetres; smaller flakes are left to the fog.
If [code]true[/code], a heightfield collider following the camera stops flakes under roofs, trees and overhangs.
The render layers the shelter heightfield sees.
The [SnowCover3D] giving the snowfall, the temperature and the snow on the ground. Empty: the active one.
The snowfall in millimetres of water an hour; negative takes it from the snowpack and the weather.
The exposure the streaks show, in seconds: each flake and grain is drawn stretched along the distance it moves in this time.
The threshold wind for blowing snow in m/s at 10 m; negative uses Li and Pomeroy's relation to the air temperature.

Push the snow's extinction to the active [WeatherMap3D] ([method WeatherMap3D.set_precipitation_extinction]): the falling snow as haze everywhere, the blowing snow as a layer over the snow around the camera. Both renderers draw it.
Scale of the turbulent eddies flakes and drifting snow ride on top of the weather wind (Kraichnan's random Fourier modes, σ = 2.5 u*).
